clue.text: I am meeting criminal person I'd put behind bars

parts.note: I am contracts to I'm

indicators.note: criminal suggests the letters are bent out of their lawful order

explanation.surface: A speaker confesses to meeting a lawbreaker they would happily see locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'person' reads as part of the definition, but it is fodder; the definition is only the last three words.
explanation.definitionFit: To be jailed is to be put behind bars, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Country one governed

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
to run a country is to govern it, so governed gives ran

explanation.surface: A nation once ruled under a single leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Iran is an example of a country in western Asia.

clue.text: Fancy study being held up after sales spiel

indicators.note: after places the study piece behind the spiel

parts.note: a salesman's patter is his spiel

indicators.note: in a down clue, held up means the word is lifted to read bottom to top

parts.note: a den is a private study

explanation.surface: Someone is kept waiting in their study by a salesman's pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Fancy, as an adjective, means decorated or patterned rather than plain.

clue.text: Country tipped to help Northern Ireland

indicators.note: tipped up in a down clue means the pieces are turned to read upwards

parts.note: to help is to aid

explanation.surface: A country is tipped to come to Northern Ireland's assistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tipped' turns AIDNI over, giving the country.
explanation.definitionFit: India is an example of a country, in south Asia.

clue.text: Hand in dictionary — it's left out

indicators.note: in puts the hand inside the dictionary's letters

parts.note: OED is the Oxford English Dictionary
mitt is slang for a hand

explanation.surface: A lexicographer hands in a dictionary and finds a word missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Omitted is a direct synonym of excluded or not included.

clue.text: Carries out belongings

definitions.meaning: to effect something is to bring it about or carry it out

explanation.surface: Someone carries their possessions out of the house.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb sense means accomplishes; the noun sense means personal possessions.

clue.text: Female with diary to sell

parts.note: a log is a daily record, a diary

explanation.surface: A woman puts her diary up for sale.
explanation.definitionFit: Flog is British slang for selling something, often cheaply.

clue.text: A romancer specialises in this position in bed?

definitions.meaning: a romancer is a teller of tall tales, so telling untruths is his speciality
being stretched out flat is how one is placed in bed

explanation.surface: A seducer's favourite pose in the bedroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'romancer' looks like a lover, but here means a fabricator of stories.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both telling falsehoods and reclining horizontally.

clue.text: Argentine novel about old age

indicators.note: about means the shuffled letters go around the O
novel means new, so the letters are made into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written for the anagram

explanation.surface: A South American novel concerns growing old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' rearranges ARGENTINE into GENERATIN, and 'about' wraps it round O.
explanation.definitionFit: A generation is a period or age, the span between parents and children.

clue.text: Holed in one around start of tournament? Player did it

indicators.note: around means the holed-in-one word goes around the letter

parts.note: to ace a golf hole is to hole in one

indicators.note: start of means only the opening letter of the tournament word is used

explanation.surface: A golfer hits a hole in one at the very beginning of a tournament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Player' looks like the golfer but is an actor.
explanation.definitionFit: A player is an actor, so what a player did on stage is perform.

clue.text: Fine tonic cured disease

indicators.note: cured means treated or processed, so the letters are worked into a new form

explanation.surface: A good tonic cleared up an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: An infection is a disease caused by germs.

clue.text: Easier to understand nurse perhaps restricting the French

indicators.note: restricting means the carer confines the French word within it

parts.note: a nurse is an example of a carer
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A nurse limits use of French so as to be better understood.
explanation.definitionFit: Something clearer is plainer, so more easily grasped.

clue.text: Lace — it's unusually stretchy

indicators.note: unusually means arranged in an unusual way, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Some lace is surprisingly stretchy.
explanation.definitionFit: Elastic material stretches and springs back, a synonym.

clue.text: Anxious period in American hospital department

indicators.note: in puts the period within the department's letters

parts.note: ER is the emergency room in an American hospital
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A worrying wait in an American emergency room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Anxious' looks like worried, but here means keen.
explanation.definitionFit: Anxious can mean keen, as in anxious to please, a synonym for keen.

clue.text: Detective's reported on being found out

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector, plus the possessive S
journalists cover a story when they report on it

explanation.surface: A detective's account is exposed when the press gets hold of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Discovered means detected or found out, a synonym.

clue.text: Snubbed westbound US soldier on retreating, blushing

indicators.note: westbound in an across clue means travelling leftward, so the letters read backwards

parts.note: GI is an American soldier

indicators.note: retreating means going back, so the little word is turned round

parts.note: a blushing face is red

explanation.surface: An American soldier heading west, embarrassed and backing off, is cold-shouldered.
explanation.definitionFit: To be snubbed is to be deliberately ignored, a synonym.

clue.text: Take away relic, even ignoring conclusions

indicators.note: ignoring conclusions means each of the two words loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone is told to remove a relic, unfinished business or not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring conclusions' drops C from RELIC and N from EVEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To relieve someone of something is to take it away from them.

clue.text: Man determined to secure right type of vehicle

indicators.note: to secure means the set word holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: set means fixed or determined
a van is a type of vehicle

explanation.surface: A resolute man makes sure he gets the correct van.
explanation.definitionFit: A man, as in manservant, is a male servant or valet.

clue.text: Digs both ends of allotment, entertaining some chaps

indicators.note: entertaining means holding as guests, so the outer letters enclose the rest
both ends of means the first and last letters of allotment

parts.note: part means some, a portion
chaps are men

explanation.surface: Some men dig over an allotment, a garden plot rented from the council.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Digs' looks like a verb about gardening, but is British slang for lodgings.
explanation.definitionFit: Digs is British slang for lodgings, and an apartment is a flat one lives in.

clue.text: Poaches fish — add leeks, regularly chopped

parts.note: a cod is a fish

indicators.note: regularly chopped means every other letter is cut out, keeping the second, fourth and so on

explanation.surface: A cookery instruction: poach fish, then add chopped leeks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poaches' looks like a cooking method, which it is: coddling eggs is cooking them gently in water.
explanation.definitionFit: To coddle eggs is to cook them gently in water just below boiling, like poaching.

clue.text: It's what's behind ham aroma mainly found on Eastern Railway

indicators.note: mainly means most of the word, so its last letter goes

parts.note: a scent is an aroma

explanation.surface: The smell of ham pervades an Eastern Railway train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ham' is a hammy, overacting actor; the backdrop on stage stands behind him.
explanation.definitionFit: Stage backdrops stand behind an actor, a ham being a showy, overacting performer.

clue.text: Storm's too darn wild

indicators.note: wild means unruly, so the letters run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: A storm is complained of as being far too wild.
explanation.definitionFit: A tornado is a violent rotating storm, an example of one.

clue.text: Threaten manoeuvres circumventing new base of operations

indicators.note: manoeuvres means moves about, signalling the remaining letters are rearranged
circumventing means getting round or avoiding, so the letter is left out

explanation.surface: Military exercises threaten to bypass something new.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circumventing' removes N from THREATEN; 'manoeuvres' rearranges THREATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre of war or operations is the region where military action is based.

clue.text: Reluctant to forget a short bit of the Bible

indicators.note: to forget means a letter is dropped, here the a named in the clue

parts.note: averse means reluctant or unwilling

explanation.surface: Someone unwilling to forget a snippet of Scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bible is divided into chapters and numbered short passages of a line or two.

clue.text: Taking spin around, quietly drive back

indicators.note: around means the spin word goes round the letter

parts.note: to reel is to spin or whirl
P is piano, the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: Turning round, a driver quietly reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: To repel attackers is to drive them back, a synonym.

clue.text: Perhaps lead part

definitions.meaning: lead, the metal, is an example of a chemical substance in the periodic table
a component or constituent is part of something

explanation.surface: Perhaps take the lead part in a play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead part' reads as a starring role, but lead is the metal Pb.
explanation.definitionFit: Lead is a chemical example of the word; separately it means a component.

clue.text: Engage in new project? Not half!

indicators.note: Not half means half the word is cut, keeping its first five letters

parts.note: an enterprise is a new venture or project

explanation.surface: Asked to take part in a new venture, someone replies with the British exclamation 'Not half!', meaning certainly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' is British slang for 'yes, very much', but here removes half the word.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter into an activity is to engage in or take part in it.

clue.text: Animal's adorable, it's said

indicators.note: it's said means the word is pronounced, giving a word sounding the same

parts.note: dear means sweet or adorable

explanation.surface: Someone remarks on how sweet a creature is.
explanation.definitionFit: Deer are an example of a hoofed animal, such as the red deer.

clue.text: The Queen returns with gift to exhibit

indicators.note: returns means the royal cipher comes back the other way

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
a present is a gift

explanation.surface: The monarch comes back bearing a gift to display.
explanation.definitionFit: To represent can mean to show or exhibit, as a painting represents a scene.

clue.text: Thread in skirt hem entangles

indicators.note: in means the letters sit inside the run of clue words

explanation.surface: A loose thread in a skirt's hem gets tangled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thread' looks like sewing cotton, but means a recurring idea.
explanation.definitionFit: A thread of an argument is its underlying subject or main idea.

clue.text: Herb could make daughter poorly

parts.note: poorly is British for unwell, ill

explanation.surface: A herbal remedy might make a daughter sick.
explanation.definitionFit: Dill is an example of a feathery culinary herb.

clue.text: Kind author that has characters making an impression

definitions.text: that has characters making an impression

parts.note: a type is a kind or sort
an author is a writer

explanation.surface: A generous novelist whose characters leave a lasting impression on readers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' are not fictional people but letters struck onto paper, each key making an impression.
explanation.definitionFit: This machine has keys bearing letters that strike an inked ribbon, imprinting text on paper.
